thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: HIGH — kv-cache eviction storm in i-rtp-prod leading to 25–40% tail latency for text-gen routes. Pager: @Maya R. oncall.

Maya R.: paging — seeing sustained 503s and latency for customer-facing routes, spike at 12:06 UTC. I’m SSHing into the gpu pool to check KV metrics.

Jon H.: on it, grabbing logs. rolling back recent kvcache tweak? which deploy touched eviction_policy?

Maya R.: @Jon H. quick check: deploy b/2025.03.12.14 changed eviction strategy. I rolled a temporary config to increase TTLs at 12:02 but not sure it applied everywhere.

Priya S.: adding context — b/2025.03.12.14 was the quant-kv-evict change (reduces memory by more aggressive LRU shards). We saw this in perf test but not at prod scale.

Sam T.: if this is causing KV churn, requests are hitting cold prefixes, huge KV reloads, TTI balloons. Can we disable eviction and revert to previous policy?

Maya R.: reverting to policy v2 now (command pasted):

```
# revert eviction policy
rkctl set kvcache --policy conservative --shards 64
```

Maya R.: revert started 12:12 — patch rolling to 8 nodes first. monitoring.

oncall-bot: Deploy rollback initiated by Maya R. — 8/8 pods acknowledged, staged rollback to remaining nodes.

Jon H.: seeing latency drop on canary nodes. customer error rate still high for 5m window but trending down.

Lucas P.: customer-impact note — reported errors from two enterprise customers: Widgetly and DataKite. Support already looped in. Need CTA for them.

Diane K.: prioritized comms: small oh-snap message to affected accounts + ETA. I can draft.

Priya S.: root cause hypothesis: eviction aggressiveness + uneven shard placement under high seq-len workloads. Action: quantify how many cache misses per-second and correlate with config.

Sam T.: created remediation ticket #INC-5942 for kvcache policy rollback + targeted tests. Assigning to Priya and Jon for triage.

Maya R.: creating postmortem and action items. Scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Who can attend?

Jon H.: I’ll be there — will bring logs and dashboard links.

Priya S.: can attend, will bring repro.

Lucas P.: product rep attending for customer impact and prioritization.

Diane K.: +1 for comms.

incident-bot: Action items added to INC-5942:
- AI-1: Collect KV miss metrics, histograms by model and seq-length (owner: Priya S., size: M).
- AI-2: Run targeted scale tests with high-seq workloads on kvcache conservative policy (owner: Jon H., size: L).
- AI-3: Add automated revert trigger when cache miss rate > 5% sustained (owner: Sam T., size: S).
- AI-4: Customer outreach + status + mitigation ETA (owner: Diane K., size: S).
- AI-5: Postmortem doc draft and action tracker (owner: Maya R., size: S).

Maya R.: quick notes on sizing rationale — S = can be done within a 2-day sprint by 1 eng; M = needs a focused 1-week effort and cross-team; L = ~2+ person-weeks or infra workload.

Priya S.: for AI-1 I’ll need historical KV metrics (last 90 days) and a synthetic generator for seq-length. Adding subtask in INC-5942.

Sam T.: for AI-3 I’ll propose a conservative threshold + cooldown and test in staging. Sizable but quick.

Lucas P.: prioritization request — these items map to severity/P1 for now because customer impact on enterprise accounts. From roadmap perspective, AI-2 and AI-1 should be in Q2 infra reliability workstream. AI-3 is a security/ops-safety quick win that we should do immediately.

Diane K.: tagging comms as P1 for customers. I’ll prepare personalized notes for Widgetly and DataKite and coordinate with account leads.

Jon H.: preliminary timeline:
- short-term (24–48h): complete rollback, monitor, customer comms (owners: Maya, Diane).
- mid-term (1–2 weeks): AI-1 and AI-3 implementation and staging tests (Priya, Sam).
- longer-term (Q2): AI-2 scale tests + shard rebalancing plan (Jon + infra).

Maya R.: adding severity labels to action items in INC-5942: AI-1 = Sev 2, AI-2 = Sev 2, AI-3 = Sev 1, AI-4 = Sev 1, AI-5 = Sev 3.

Priya S.: question — Sev mapping looks good. For Q2 planning, can we tag AI-2 as sprint candidate for next planning cycle? Jon?

Jon H.: yes, I’ll push AI-2 into the reliability backlog for the Q2 sprint planning board and add estimates.

Lucas P.: product ask — tie AI-2 into the customer SLA initiative. If we can reduce tail latency by 15% under heavy seq-len, we should include it as an SLA improvement metric.

Diane K.: timeline for comms ETA to accounts: initial update within 2 hours, detailed follow-up after rollback verification (EOD).

Maya R.: rollback fully applied 12:18 UTC. Latency back to baseline at 12:20. Marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — mitigation: policy rollback. Postmortem scheduled: 2025-03-13 16:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).

Sam T.: created RFC stub for automated revert triggers and put in /eng-infra for early feedback.

Priya S.: will upload KV histograms and the minimal repro to the postmortem doc before the meeting.

Jon H.: note for postmortem: capture what tests missed this and why the canary didn't exercise the scale pattern.

Lucas P.: will prepare customer impact slides and escalate to account execs once Diane's notes are ready.

Diane K.: draft posted to the incident doc — please review and comment: https://redwood.sap/pm/INC-5942/comm-draft

Maya R.: final checklist for postmortem:
1) Timeline + impact — (Maya)
2) Root cause and evidence — (Priya + Jon)
3) Action items + owners + sizing — (Maya)
4) Customer comms summary — (Diane)
5) Q2 backlog tie-ins — (Lucas + Jon)

Maya R.: anything else?

Lucas P.: maybe add discussion point on improved canary/chaos tests for kvcache churn.

Jon H.: +1, add to AI-2 scope.

Diane K.: thx all. I’ll send the initial customer notes now. :thumbsup:

Maya R.: thanks team — great quick reaction. See you at the postmortem.

incident-bot: Thread closed for updates; please add follow-ups to INC-5942.
